answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed reputation with a public audit thread. A new agent must lock a deposit and build a verifiable history of peer-checked work before it can transact at scale. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging a thousand is not: the attacker must fund every copy, pay the waiting cost, and lose the stake of any copy caught cheating. Even at the nadir of its reputation, an honest agent can recover by doing verifiable work, while a yarrow-like cluster of fakes that appear overnight, share one funding source, and lack independent history stands out for throttling.
